concurrency_and_state: Static singleton GameScr.instance (clearGameScr sets instance = null at GameScr.cs:1966-1969) coexists with dozens of static fields (vCharInMap, vMob, vNpc, vItemMap, sks, parts, efs, arrs, darts, onScreenSkill, keySkill, ~35 isPaint* booleans, camera cmx/cmy, isAutoPlay), which are not reset by clearGameScr() and risk stale state across relog/server switches.

Shared static MyVector collections (vCharInMap, vMob, vNpc, vItemMap, vMobAttack, vChatVip) and static state flags (isPaintOther, isAutoPlay, isLoadAllData) have no synchronization between packet-handling updates and UI/game loop reads.

Static field initializers at GameScr.cs:571-573 eagerly call mSystem.loadImage("/mainImage/i_pve_bar_0.png") and i_pve_bar_1.png at class load time, duplicating loads in loadBg() (GameScr.cs:1176-1177).
cross_module_questions: Does Service.gI().changeOnKeyScr(sbyte[]) distinguish between onScreenSkill and keySkill, or does saveKeySkillToRMS() (GameScr.cs:1535-1550) overwrite/conflict with saveonScreenSkillToRMS() (GameScr.cs:1518-1533) when addSkillShortcut() calls both sequentially (GameScr.cs:1579-1580)?

Does the server validate Char.myCharz() position updates sent via Service.gI().charMove() when GameScr.isAttack() teleports cx/cy client-side during melee range adjustment (GameScr.cs:2590-2640, 2683-2686, 2779-2792)?
Where is GameScr.getMaxExp(int level) called, and does any caller break when getMaxExp returns a truncated/overflowed int from long[] exps (GameScr.cs:1345-1353)?

Does the server send >255 ItemOptionTemplate entries or skill IDs >= 512 in NRitem0 / NR_skill RMS payloads, which would trigger truncation in loadOptionTemplatesFromRMS() (GameScr.cs:239) or stream desync in readSkill() (GameScr.cs:1888)?

findings.impact: High coupling across camera, HUD textures, RMS binary parsers, entity lists, combat targeting, trade state, and event UI makes changes risky and hard to isolate; clearGameScr() leaves static state behind.
findings.root_cause: GameScr (8333 lines) acts as a monolithic God Class storing ~100+ static fields (entity MyVectors, ~35 isPaint* booleans, Image assets, templates, camera coordinates, trade/event/auto-play state) alongside instance combat/input state.
findings.title: God Class architecture with extensive unreset static state in GameScr

findings.impact: If any skill in NR_skill has id >= sks.Length (e.g., >= max(512, num + 100)), the binary stream position becomes misaligned, causing all subsequent skills to read garbage bytes or throw EOFException, and id 1111 can overwrite sks[num - 1].
findings.root_cause: In readSkill(), when num3 < 0 or num3 >= sks.Length, the if-block (line 1888) skips reading effectHappenOnMob, numEff, skillStand, and skillfly bytes instead of consuming them from DataInputStream. Also line 1884 remaps num3 == 1111 to (short)(num - 1) without collision protection.
findings.title: Stream desync in readSkill() when skill ID exceeds sks array bounds

findings.impact: In saveKeySkillToRMS(), keySkill is sent using the exact same Service.changeOnKeyScr(array) call as saveonScreenSkillToRMS(); calling both in addSkillShortcut() causes the second call to overwrite the first or lose keySkill bindings.
findings.root_cause: saveKeySkillToRMS() invokes Service.gI().changeOnKeyScr(array) instead of a keySkill-specific method/parameter, mirroring saveonScreenSkillToRMS().
findings.title: saveKeySkillToRMS() calls changeOnKeyScr identical to saveonScreenSkillToRMS()

findings.impact: On servers where cumulative EXP exceeds int.MaxValue (~2.14B), getMaxExp returns negative or wrapped values, corrupting level/EXP bar calculations and displays.
findings.root_cause: exps is declared as long[], but getMaxExp(int level) returns int and accumulates num += (int)exps[i] without checked arithmetic or bounds/null validation on exps.
findings.title: Integer overflow in getMaxExp(int level) when summing long[] exps into int

findings.impact: When NR_arrow RMS data is missing or null, readArrow() throws an exception and then throws a secondary NullReferenceException in finally when calling dataInputStream.close().
findings.root_cause: readArrow() passes Rms.loadRMS("NR_arrow") directly to new DataInputStream(...) without a null check, and calls dataInputStream.close() in finally without checking dataInputStream != null.
findings.title: Missing null checks in readArrow() cause NullReferenceException in finally

findings.impact: DataInputStream in loadOptionTemplatesFromRMS() is never closed (resource leak), and readUnsignedByte() truncates template counts if count > 255.
findings.root_cause: loadOptionTemplatesFromRMS() creates DataInputStream at line 233 without a finally/close() block, and reads count using d.readUnsignedByte() at line 239.
findings.title: Unclosed DataInputStream and 8-bit count limit in loadOptionTemplatesFromRMS()

findings.impact: Calling playerMenu(Char c) when charFocus or myskill is null throws NullReferenceException; also checkClickToBotton/PvP positioning in isAttack() can snap player into walls or onto unexpected Y coordinates without collision checks.
findings.root_cause: playerMenu(Char c) ignores parameter c and directly dereferences Char.myCharz().charFocus.charID and Char.myCharz().myskill.template.type without null guards. In isAttack(), PvP separation (lines 2779-2792) and NPC Y-snap (lines 2683-2686) directly mutate Char.myCharz().cx/cy without tile collision checks (unlike mob separation at lines 2597-2628).
findings.title: NullReferenceException risk in playerMenu() and unguarded client teleport in isAttack()

findings.impact: Attacking/clicking a mob forces isAutoPlay = true even when the mob cannot be attacked or the player is blocked by captcha or invalid skill state.
findings.root_cause: isAttack() sets isAutoPlay = true at line 2491 before validating isMeCanAttackMob, mobCapcha == null, myskill != null, and checkSkillValid().
findings.title: isAutoPlay enabled prematurely in isAttack() before attack validity checks

findings.impact: On screens where width != height, gW23 is miscalculated from screen height gH, potentially distorting UI/camera offsets that depend on gW23; loadCamera also reads Rms.loadRMSInt("viewchat") twice.
findings.root_cause: loadCamera() assigns gW23 = gH - 120 instead of using gW, and evaluates Rms.loadRMSInt("viewchat") twice instead of caching the return value in a local variable.
findings.title: gW23 computed from gH and duplicate RMS read in loadCamera()

findings.impact: Every out-of-range attack tick allocates new MovePoint and Command objects, and missing/corrupt RMS files log Cout.LogError (creating red Console error badges in Unity) even when fallback/re-fetch is handled.
findings.root_cause: isAttack() instantiates new MovePoint(...) and new Command(null, null, 8002, null) repeatedly while approaching targets; RMS loaders emit Cout.LogError on parse/load failures.
findings.title: Repeated object allocations in isAttack() and LogError usage in RMS loaders

key_classes.name: GameScr
key_classes.responsibility: Central gameplay screen (God Class) managing camera/viewport layout, HUD textures, RMS binary asset/template loading, entity vector lists, skill shortcut bars, player interaction menus, and melee/ranged auto-approach & attack targeting.

module_summary: Lines 1-2835 of GameScr.cs define the core state and setup of the main in-game screen God Class: static HUD/entity/UI-flag fields, RMS binary template loaders (NRitem0, NR_part, NR_effect, NR_arrow, NR_dart, NR_skill), skill shortcut slot management (onScreenSkill/keySkill), camera & responsive touch/PC UI layout (loadCamera/updateCamera/setSkillBarPosition), and target interaction/attack routing (playerMenu, isAttack).

protocol_touchpoints.payload_summary: vcItem (byte), type (byte), count (unsigned byte), followed by count * (name UTF, type byte) for ItemOptionTemplate.
num (short), followed by num * (type byte, pi.Length * (id short, dx byte, dy byte)) for character/item Parts.
num (short), followed by num * (idEf short, arrEfInfoLen byte, arrEfInfoLen * (idImg short, dx byte, dy byte)).
num (short), followed by num * (id short, imgId[0..2] 3x short).
num (short), followed by num * (id, nUpdate, va*256, xdPercent, tail[], tailBorder[], xd1[], xd2[], head[][], headBorder[][]) all short-length prefixed shorts.
num (short), followed by num * (id short, effectHappenOnMob short, numEff byte, skillStand[], skillfly[] with status byte + 12 shorts each).
